patch.description:
fgos discover overwrites a locked verify command: resolveDiscovery in src/intake/discovery.mjs writes verdict.verify from judgeDiscovery's own model guess straight onto work.verify with no check for whether a prior session already set a real, locked verify command there. Concretely: tsk-5e97 (2026-08-02) went through fgos-exploring/fgos-planning/fgos-validating first, and fgos-validating explicitly set item.verify to a real, narrow, already-passing command (node --test test/intake/decompose.test.mjs) and locked it in plan.md's Proof-surface section. Only afterward did the session realize fgos-exploring's own CONTEXT.md lock had never actually been released through the discover verb, so it ran "fgos discover tsk-5e97" -- and that call's own judgeDiscovery verdict carried a DIFFERENT, broader verify guess ("npm test", the whole suite) which resolveDiscovery wrote over the already-locked, already-correct value with no warning. The first "fgos return" then re-ran that broad "npm test" and failed on 2 pre-existing unrelated repo tests, moving the item to blocked -- a false-negative return failure caused entirely by the overwrite, not by the item's actual implementation (64/64 on the correct narrow command). Fix scope is likely in resolveDiscovery/judgeDiscovery's verify-handling in src/intake/discovery.mjs: either never overwrite an existing non-empty/non-placeholder work.verify with the model's own guess, or only fill it when the field is empty/placeholder, mirroring how a locked CONTEXT.md is already treated as a stronger trust signal than a fresh model guess elsewhere in the same file (see readLockedContext's docstring in decompose.mjs, reused by discovery.mjs's own resolveDiscovery per tsk-ozl D2).

ROOT CAUSE traced (this session, live-reproduced on tsk-3sw, not speculation): the overwrite happens because the tsk-ozl D2 skip shortcut (readLockedContext) is structurally dead code for the standard interactive workflow, in BOTH resolveDiscovery AND resolveDecompose -- so judgeDiscovery ALWAYS runs (never skipped), which is why its verify guess is always what reaches the overwrite site this item already describes.

Both resolveDiscovery (discovery.mjs:518-519) and resolveDecompose (decompose.mjs:438-439) compute 'const repoRoot = path.dirname(dir)' where dir is always the main checkout's .fgos (required by --dir, since worktrees never carry their own .fgos per ADR0020), then call readLockedContext(repoRoot, work.docsRef) -- a plain fs.readFileSync (no git-awareness) against path.join(repoRoot, docsRef). But fgos-exploring/fgos-planning write and COMMIT CONTEXT.md/plan.md to the item's OWN fgw/<id> branch/worktree (their own hard rule: commit before calling fgos discover) -- not to main, which has no idea those files exist until later merge. So readLockedContext always reads from the wrong physical directory and always finds nothing, in exactly the scenario (interactive session already did the real reasoning) the shortcut exists to serve. Confirmed live for tsk-3sw: after fgos-exploring committed CONTEXT.md and got contextApprove approved, 'fgos discover tsk-3sw' still spawned a full nested judgeDiscovery call instead of skipping, producing a wrong verify guess (a docs-grep check for what was really a code change) that had to be manually corrected -- this item's own overwrite bug, caught live in a second, independent real case.

Same session, 'fgos decompose tsk-3sw' independently confirmed resolveDecompose has the identical repoRoot bug (lockedContext empty -- confirmed by grepping plan.md/CONTEXT.md for 'tiny'/'small', zero matches, so decompose.mjs:469's mode-skip branch could not have fired) and fell through to a real judgeDecompose call (decompose.mjs:549, verdict.kind === 'pass-through') that happened to coincidentally agree with the human-approved plan -- luck, not a plumbing guarantee. Notably, decompose.mjs itself does NOT have this item's own overwrite bug: it computes planApproveVerify ONCE (line 431, gates[id].planApprove.verify ?? work.verify) and uses it unconditionally at every moveStage-to-executing call site (lines 469, 549, 597) regardless of skip-vs-real-judge path -- decompose.mjs already does correctly what this item's fix scope should make discovery.mjs also do.

Why the existing test suite (2366 passing) never caught the repoRoot bug: test/intake/discovery.test.mjs's own mkLockedContextFixture helper builds its CONTEXT.md fixture as path.dirname(storeDir)'s child -- deliberately constructing repoRoot == content-root by fixture design, with its own comment stating this 'exactly matches readLockedContext's real path.join(repoRoot, docsRef) resolution'. The fixture validates the function's internal logic in isolation; it never models the real git-worktree topology (state root always main per ADR0020, content root the item's own separate fgw/<id> checkout) that breaks it in production.

Widened fix scope (was discovery.mjs-only, now both files): resolveDiscovery AND resolveDecompose need to read CONTEXT.md/plan.md from the caller's actual live working directory (the worktree an interactive fgos-exploring/fgos-planning session is standing in) rather than deriving a content-root from the state-root dir/--dir -- likely an explicit separate parameter threaded through resolveDiscovery/resolveDecompose/readLockedContext, distinct from dir (which must keep resolving state from main per ADR0020). This item's own original fix idea (never overwrite a non-empty/non-placeholder work.verify) is a valid, narrower complementary guard -- but fixing repoRoot is the deeper fix, since it also restores the skip path's real purpose (avoiding the wasteful/context-blind judge call entirely, not just protecting verify from it). Test fixtures for both files need a new test shape separating repoRoot-for-content from dir-for-state -- the existing fixture's coincidental repoRoot==content-root construction must not be the only test evidence going forward.

Capacity dispatch: simplify kind resolution default branch (prefer native Task tool when a live session already has it; else spawn claude --agent). Today capacities.<id>.kind has 'cli' (real cli-spawn adapter) and 'task' (declared in CAPACITY_KINDS, zero working differentiation -- resolves through the same command/args spawn path as cli, functionally identical to cli today).

CORRECTION (supersedes earlier wrong claim in this item's history): 'claude -p' CAN run as a specific named agent definition headlessly -- confirmed via 'claude --help': '--agent <agent> Agent for the current session. Overrides the agent setting.' This means a kind:'task' capacity is NOT structurally blocked for cli-dispatch/spawnWorker as earlier claimed. resolveExecutorConfig can build real command/args for an agentType-only capacity too: command:'claude', args including '-p','{prompt}','--agent',<agentType>,'--model','{model}' (plus whatever --allowedTools/--permission-mode the global default template already uses) -- spawned via the EXISTING cli-spawn adapter, no new EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS entry needed, no resolve-time fail-loud for a missing command/args when agentType is present. This works identically for BOTH cli-dispatch (spawnWorker, headless) and task-dispatch (resolveCapacityCli, in-session) -- the earlier 'signal-return instead of command, only for task-dispatch' design is WRONG and retracted.

Revised design (recommended direction, not yet finalized): resolveCapacityCli's return shape does NOT need to be kind-discriminated after all. It can uniformly keep returning {command,args,provider,model} for every capacity, cli or task alike -- for a kind:'task' capacity with no own command/args, resolveExecutorCommand derives command/args from the global default executor template plus an inserted '--agent',<agentType> pair (new code needed: today's fallthrough only reuses executor/executors.<tier> args verbatim, has no notion of inserting an extra flag). The calling skill (task-dispatch consumer, per docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md's pattern) then applies its OWN optional optimization: if it already has live Agent/Task tool access AND the capacity's kind is 'task', it MAY call the Task tool natively instead of exec'ing the resolved command (cheaper -- no subprocess startup -- and observable, per the original agent-terminal transparency goal that started this whole discussion) -- but exec'ing the resolved command is always a valid, correct fallback either way, since both paths produce the same semantic outcome (right agent definition + right model on the prompt). This removes almost all the earlier signal-vs-exec branching complexity from resolveCapacityCli itself and pushes the 'use Task natively when cheap' decision to the skill-side optimization layer, where it belongs (the skill already self-knows its own tool manifest).

Validation (static, config-load time, validateCapacityShape): unchanged plan -- 'agentType', when present, must be a non-empty string, same optional-field pattern as 'model'/'allowCrossProvider' today. No kind-based requirement enforced statically (a single capacities.<id> entry's config is validated once but may be resolved via either path across its lifetime). The earlier proposed 'resolve-time fail-loud in cli-dispatch when kind:task has no command/args' is RETRACTED -- no longer needed, since --agent flag always gives cli-dispatch a real way to resolve it.

Still open, not yet resolved:
1. judge-discovery-style capacity that already declares BOTH kind:'task' AND its own explicit command/args (today's real .fgos-runner.json entry) -- when resolved via task-dispatch, does resolveExecutorConfig's existing precedence (capacity's own command/args wins) still apply unchanged? Likely yes (no special-case needed, byCapacity already wins over derived-from-agentType-template) but not yet traced through code.
2. Model precedence between capacity's tier-derived model (modelForTier/capacity.model) and the named agent definition's own pinned model in its .claude/agents/<name>.md frontmatter (tsk-slq) -- '--model {model}' on the CLI flag path would override whatever the agent file pins, same as today's global executor already does; but native Task tool call's own model param vs. the subagent definition's pinned model precedence is a separate, still-untraced question.
3. judge-decompose gap -- FIXED, commit 784bcbc (widened executors.judge's --allowedTools in .fgos/config.json to Task,WebSearch,WebFetch,Read, matching judge-discovery's own override; also fixed 3 live docs still pointing only at the now-legacy .fgos-runner.json instead of .fgos/config.json's runner section, and re-applied the domain-1/domain-2 -> cli-dispatch/task-dispatch rename in dispatch.mjs/its test after a branch switch had reverted it). No longer open, unaffected by this item's own remaining scope.

Design record continuity: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md.

Traced (confirmed via code read, resolveExecutorConfig in src/runner/dispatch.mjs, not speculation): 'const byCapacity = capacity && (capacity.adapter || capacity.command) ? capacity : undefined; const executor = byCapacity ?? perTier ?? cfg.executor;' -- capacity.kind is NEVER read by this precedence chain. It is only read in two OTHER, separate checks, both gated on kind === 'cli': the fgosDir presence-check, and the cross-provider governance check. kind:'task' triggers neither -- zero resolve-time validation exists for task kind today.

This confirms open question 1 (judge-discovery-style precedence): a capacity declaring BOTH kind:'task' AND its own command/args (like judge-discovery today) always resolves to that own command/args via byCapacity, unconditionally, identically for cli-dispatch and task-dispatch -- both call the exact same resolveExecutorConfig function, no path-based branching exists inside it at all (fgosDir presence/absence only toggles the kind:'cli' presence-check, nothing else).

This also PROVES the risk tsk-3sw already flagged about the planned agentType field: byCapacity's condition checks ONLY 'capacity.adapter || capacity.command' -- it has NO clause for 'capacity.agentType'. So an agentType-only capacity (kind:'task', no command/args, per this item's planned design) would compute byCapacity = undefined today and silently fall through to perTier/global executor, dropping agentType entirely with no error. Concrete required code change (not yet implemented): the byCapacity condition must become 'capacity.adapter || capacity.command || capacity.agentType', with a new branch that derives command:'claude' + args including '--agent', capacity.agentType (built from the global default executor's own args template, per this item's earlier '--agent flag' correction) when only agentType is present.

Model precedence (open question 2) -- RESOLVED empirically, real evidence, not speculation: ran 'claude -p --agent code-simplifier --model haiku --debug-file <log> "say hi"' and grepped the debug log's real dispatched API model field. With '--model haiku' present: log shows 'dispatching to firstParty model=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' -- the explicit --model flag WINS over code-simplifier's own pinned 'model: opus' frontmatter. Re-ran with '--agent code-simplifier' alone, no --model flag: log shows 'dispatching to firstParty model=claude-opus-5' -- confirms the agent definition's own pinned model is the fallback default when --model is omitted. (Also confirmed separately, before this: '--agent code-simplifier' genuinely loads the right persona -- asked it to quote its own system prompt, got back the real code-simplifier.md persona text and matching tool list, so --agent resolution itself works as expected.)

Confirmed precedence chain: explicit '--model' CLI flag > agent definition's own pinned 'model:' frontmatter (used only when --model is omitted from args).

Resulting open design decision (not yet resolved, this is now a real choice, not an unknown): when building args for an agentType-only capacity (this item's planned '--agent' flag support), should the args template unconditionally include '--model {model}' (from tier/capacity.model, like today's global default executor template always does) -- meaning the capacity's own configured tier always overrides whatever model the named agent definition pins for itself? Or should it OMIT '--model' for agentType capacities, letting the agent definition's own pinned model win, since presumably whoever authored that agent definition (e.g. code-simplifier pinning opus) already made a deliberate model choice for that persona that a work item's generic tier shouldn't silently override? Needs a decision before implementation, not an assumption either way.

IMPORTANT constraint discovered, must shape this item's implementation (see tsk-53h for full evidence, verified live): the planned 'agentType' capacity field must NOT be built Claude-only. 'agy' (already a real cli-dispatch target in this repo, submit-assist-classify) has its OWN independent '--agent <name>' persona-dispatch mechanism + its own 'agent.md' custom-agent file format (different frontmatter schema than Claude's '.claude/agents/<name>.md' -- agy: mainAgent/subagent/hidden/inheritMcp/commandExecutionPolicy/model; Claude: name/description/model/tools). Both CLIs happen to share the flag NAMES '--agent'/'--model' (coincidental, not a shared schema). Verified live: 'agy --model gemini-3.6-flash-high --agent default -p ...' works today.

Design consequence for this item: resolveExecutorConfig's planned args-building for an agentType-only capacity (this item's earlier '--agent flag' correction) cannot assume the executor.command is always 'claude' -- it must build the '--agent'/agent-definition-lookup step per the RESOLVED executor.command (claude vs agy vs any future provider with its own equivalent), or explicitly scope this item to Claude-only for now and file the agy/multi-provider generalization as separate follow-on scope (tsk-slq's canonical agents/<name>.yaml -> per-provider adapter projection idea, tracked in tsk-53h). Needs an explicit scope decision before implementation: build Claude-only now (simpler, matches today's only real agentType precedent, judge-discovery) and file agy-adapter support as future work, OR design the per-provider mapping now. Leaning Claude-only-now per YAGNI (no concrete agy-agentType consumer exists yet, unlike judge-discovery's real Claude case) -- but flagging explicitly rather than silently assuming, since it changes resolveExecutorConfig's shape (single hardcoded '--agent' flag literal vs a provider-keyed lookup).

Host-access detection for task-dispatch resolve (discussed, empirically checked, not yet acted on in code): live env inspection in an actual Claude Code session ('env | grep -iE claude') confirms 'CLAUDECODE' (and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT/CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/etc.) really is set by the claude CLI binary itself on startup -- but no env var exposes the session's own allowedTools/permission list (checked: 'env | grep -iE TOOL|ALLOWED|PERMISSION' empty), so no env-based signal can tell task-dispatch's resolve step whether Task/Agent tool is ACTUALLY usable right now, only whether SOME Claude Code process is running at all. Conclusion reached: no code-level host-type detection module is needed. For task-dispatch (resolveCapacityCli, run via the calling skill's own Bash tool call): the calling LLM session already inherently knows its own tool manifest (whether it has Agent/Task tool) with zero code -- self-awareness, not env-var detection -- this is exactly the 'skill-side optimization layer' decision already recorded above (native Task vs exec the resolved command). CLAUDECODE's only remaining use is as a cheap guard: absent means the resolve call is happening OUTSIDE any Claude Code process at all (a plain terminal, cron, non-Claude harness) -- there, even suggesting 'you could use Task' is nonsensical, so resolution should never even hint at kind:'task' semantics in that case, always resolve straight to cli-equivalent args. Not yet wired into any actual code -- a design conclusion to apply during this item's implementation, not a separate open question.

Vision reference (docs/decisions/0026-vision-orchestrator-roottask-capacity-native-vs-cli-spawn.md): this item's agentType/--agent-flag work is rule 4's valid exception (config forces same-provider cli/spawn) in the broader orchestrator/rootTask/capacity dispatch vision -- not superseded, one legitimate piece of that larger picture. Read 0026 before extending this item's own scope further.

task-dispatch (in-session Agent/Task tool) has no path to a non-Claude backend at all -- Claude Code's own Agent/Task tool only selects among Claude models (opus/sonnet/haiku via an agent definition's model field), never an external CLI. So a cross-provider 'cheap capacity' need inside a live session cannot route through the Agent tool by construction; the only real mechanism is shelling out to an external CLI directly -- i.e. reusing cli-dispatch's own resolveCapacityCli/spawn mechanism via Bash, exactly what fgos-submit-assist's own classify step (tsk-5l2) already does once wired. This narrows the gap originally filed here (previously framed as 'task-dispatch needs its own separate architecture, distinct from cli-dispatch') -- it does not: task-dispatch for a Claude-family choice uses the Agent tool (agent definitions' own model field already covers this), task-dispatch for a cross-provider choice reuses cli-dispatch's existing spawn mechanism via Bash, same as fgos-submit-assist already proves works. The real, narrower gap: fgos-submit-assist is the only skill wired this way today -- there is no general, reusable pattern/helper any OTHER skill could follow to declare 'shell out to this capacityId via Bash if configured+present, else fall back to a real Agent/Task subagent spawn' without re-deriving fgos-submit-assist's own wiring from scratch. Scope: extract that pattern (a shared how-to or a small skill-facing helper) so future skills don't rebuild it ad hoc. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md (fgos-submit-assist's own real precedent to generalize from).

cli-dispatch <-> task-dispatch relationship (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the two are NOT two independent, parallel mechanisms -- they nest, asymmetrically. task-dispatch can always fall through to cli-dispatch (a live session always has Bash, so shelling out to a resolved capacity command is always available -- this is the D1 mechanism above). The reverse is conditional, not structural: cli-dispatch (fgos-runner, a bare Node process, never itself inside a Claude Code session) can never call the Agent/Task tool directly -- but if the specific command it spawns IS 'claude' itself (not a different CLI like agy/gemini), that spawned process is a REAL Claude Code agent loop, and task-dispatch (Task/Agent tool use) becomes available again one level down, inside that worker -- gated entirely by whatever --allowedTools the spawned invocation was given. Today's own committed .fgos-runner.json scopes every executor's --allowedTools narrowly (e.g. 'Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)' for the default worker) -- deliberately excluding Task/Agent tool access for spawned workers today, a config choice, not a hard technical wall. A CLI other than 'claude' (agy, gemini, ...) can never nest task-dispatch at all, regardless of config -- Task/Agent tool is specific to the Claude Code harness, not a generic capability other CLIs share.

Generalizing the nesting rule beyond Claude (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the "cli-dispatch spawns a real agent harness, so task-dispatch-like nesting becomes available one level down" property is not Claude-specific by nature -- it's just that Claude Code is the only harness fgOS currently knows to have it (via Task/Agent tool, gated by --allowedTools). agy/codex are already valid, ordinary cli-dispatch spawn targets today (agy is the running submit-assist-classify example; codex is already in KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES) -- that's their normal role, no special case needed. If either ever ships its own internal subagent/tool-dispatch mechanism (its own equivalent of Task/Agent tool), the same nesting principle would extend to it: that capability would become available one level down inside that spawn, gated by whatever permission/scope equivalent that harness exposes -- the fix would be recognizing it (mirroring how kind:"task" was carved out specifically for Claude's own mechanism in CAPACITY_KINDS), not redesigning the dispatch model. Not a need to build now -- pinned so a future session doesn't have to re-derive whether the nesting rule is Claude-only by accident or by design (it's the latter: Claude-only today because Claude is the only harness with the property, not because the rule itself assumes Claude).

Correction to the nesting framing above (discovered via 'claude --help'): cli-dispatch is not limited to nested one-level Task access via a plain 'claude -p' spawn -- 'claude' CLI has a real '--agent <agent>' flag ('Agent for the current session. Overrides the agent setting.'), letting cli-dispatch spawn 'claude -p --agent <name> ...' directly, running that named agent definition (.claude/agents/<name>.md, tsk-slq's canonical root) headlessly with no Task/Agent tool nesting needed at all. So for a Claude-family agentType capacity specifically, cli-dispatch and task-dispatch now converge on the SAME achievable outcome (right agent definition + right model on the prompt) -- native Task tool (when the calling session already has it) stays the cheaper/observable choice, but exec'ing 'claude --agent <name>' is always a correct, structurally-available fallback, not a degraded one. See tsk-3sw (dependency of this item) for the concrete resolveCapacityCli/resolveExecutorConfig change this enables.

Shared-helper format preference (decided in discussion, tsk-3sw's follow-on): prefer a single shared skill-facing fragment/reference file (e.g. under .claude/skills/_shared/ or equivalent canonical path) that consumer SKILL.md files point to by path, over each skill copy-pasting the branching prose into its own SKILL.md. Reason: N independent copies drift out of sync the next time this pattern's logic changes (DRY) -- a single referenced source doesn't. Sequencing: write this helper against tsk-3sw's finished resolveCapacityCli return shape (uniform {command,args,provider,model} for both cli and task kind, per tsk-3sw's current description) -- not before that lands.

UPDATE to 'Generalizing the nesting rule beyond Claude' above (real, verified evidence -- supersedes that paragraph's 'if either ever ships its own... mechanism' framing, which was written as a future hypothetical; it is NOT hypothetical, it already exists today): 'agy' (a real, installed, multi-provider CLI already used by submit-assist-classify) has its OWN native persona-dispatch mechanism, independent of Claude's. Verified live: 'agy --help' shows '--agent' flag and 'agent'/'agents' subcommands ('List available agents'). 'agy changelog' confirms: v1.1.1 added '--agent' flag + agent/agents subcommand; v1.1.6 added 'Custom Agents (Markdown Format)' -- agy's own 'agent.md' files, YAML frontmatter with fields 'mainAgent'/'subagent'/'hidden'/'inheritMcp'/'commandExecutionPolicy'/'model' -- a DIFFERENT schema than Claude's '.claude/agents/<name>.md' (name/description/model/tools). Ran live: 'agy --model gemini-3.6-flash-high --agent default -p "..."' -- works, self-identifies as running on Gemini 3.6 Flash under agy's 'default' built-in persona. 'agy models' confirms real multi-provider model list: gemini-3.x variants, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6-thinking, gpt-oss-120b -- all reachable through the same '--agent'/'--model' flag pair.

Implication: the canonical agent-definition root (agents/<name>.yaml, tsk-slq) now has a genuine SECOND real projection target, not just Claude's '.claude/agents/'. Both agy and claude happen to share the same CLI flag NAMES ('--agent <name>', '--model <name>') -- convenient but coincidental -- while their underlying agent-definition FILE SCHEMAS differ (Claude: name/description/model/tools; agy: mainAgent/subagent/hidden/inheritMcp/commandExecutionPolicy/model). Any capacity-dispatch design that resolves an 'agentType' into CLI args (tsk-3sw) must NOT hardcode Claude-only '--agent'/'.claude/agents/' assumptions -- it needs a per-provider mapping from canonical agent definition -> that provider's own adapter format and flag syntax, exactly the projection tsk-slq's design already anticipated, now with a real second target to build against instead of a hypothetical one. Not scoped to build now (still bigger than this item's own narrower helper-pattern scope) -- pinned so a future session sees this as confirmed fact, not speculation.

THIRD real per-provider agent-dispatch shape confirmed (user-provided, sourced from official Codex docs, spot-checked live: 'codex exec --help' shows no '--agent'/'--agenttype' flag at all, matching the claim) -- 'codex' (already in KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES, installed on this machine) has a STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT agent-dispatch mechanism than both Claude and agy: no CLI flag selects the agent at all. Persona dispatch happens via PROMPT TEXT naming the agent ('Use the reviewer agent to review this branch against main...'), after defining it in '.codex/agents/<name>.toml' (TOML, fields: name/description/model/model_reasoning_effort/sandbox_mode/developer_instructions -- a THIRD distinct schema, different from both Claude's .claude/agents/<name>.md (name/description/model/tools) and agy's agent.md (mainAgent/subagent/hidden/inheritMcp/commandExecutionPolicy/model)). Built-in agents (no file needed): default/worker/explorer. cli-dispatch <-> task-dispatch relationship (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the two are NOT two independent, parallel mechanisms -- they nest, asymmetrically. task-dispatch can always fall through to cli-dispatch (a live session always has Bash, so shelling out to a resolved capacity command is always available -- this is the D1 mechanism above). The reverse is conditional, not structural: cli-dispatch (fgos-runner, a bare Node process, never itself inside a Claude Code session) can never call the Agent/Task tool directly -- but if the specific command it spawns IS 'claude' itself (not a different CLI like agy/gemini), that spawned process is a REAL Claude Code agent loop, and task-dispatch (Task/Agent tool use) becomes available again one level down, inside that worker -- gated entirely by whatever --allowedTools the spawned invocation was given. Today's own committed .fgos-runner.json scopes every executor's --allowedTools narrowly (e.g. 'Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)' for the default worker) -- deliberately excluding Task/Agent tool access for spawned workers today, a config choice, not a hard technical wall. A CLI other than 'claude' (agy, gemini, ...) can never nest task-dispatch at all, regardless of config -- Task/Agent tool is specific to the Claude Code harness, not a generic capability other CLIs share.

Generalizing the nesting rule beyond Claude (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the "cli-dispatch spawns a real agent harness, so task-dispatch-like nesting becomes available one level down" property is not Claude-specific by nature -- it's just that Claude Code is the only harness fgOS currently knows to have it (via Task/Agent tool, gated by --allowedTools). agy/codex are already valid, ordinary cli-dispatch spawn targets today (agy is the running submit-assist-classify example; codex is already in KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES) -- that's their normal role, no special case needed. If either ever ships its own internal subagent/tool-dispatch mechanism (its own equivalent of Task/Agent tool), the same nesting principle would extend to it: that capability would become available one level down inside that spawn, gated by whatever permission/scope equivalent that harness exposes -- the fix would be recognizing it (mirroring how kind:"task" was carved out specifically for Claude's own mechanism in CAPACITY_KINDS), not redesigning the dispatch model. Not a need to build now -- pinned so a future session doesn't have to re-derive whether the nesting rule is Claude-only by accident or by design (it's the latter: Claude-only today because Claude is the only harness with the property, not because the rule itself assumes Claude).

fgos discover overwrites a locked verify command: resolveDiscovery in src/intake/discovery.mjs writes verdict.verify from judgeDiscovery's own model guess straight onto work.verify with no check for whether a prior session already set a real, locked verify command there. Concretely: tsk-5e97 (2026-08-02) went through fgos-exploring/fgos-planning/fgos-validating first, and fgos-validating explicitly set item.verify to a real, narrow, already-passing command (node --test test/intake/decompose.test.mjs) and locked it in plan.md's Proof-surface section. Only afterward did the session realize fgos-exploring's own CONTEXT.md lock had never actually been released through the discover verb, so it ran "fgos discover tsk-5e97" -- and that call's own judgeDiscovery verdict carried a DIFFERENT, broader verify guess ("npm test", the whole suite) which resolveDiscovery wrote over the already-locked, already-correct value with no warning. The first "fgos return" then re-ran that broad "npm test" and failed on 2 pre-existing unrelated repo tests, moving the item to blocked -- a false-negative return failure caused entirely by the overwrite, not by the item's actual implementation (64/64 on the correct narrow command). Fix scope is likely in resolveDiscovery/judgeDiscovery's verify-handling in src/intake/discovery.mjs: either never overwrite an existing non-empty/non-placeholder work.verify with the model's own guess, or only fill it when the field is empty/placeholder, mirroring how a locked CONTEXT.md is already treated as a stronger trust signal than a fresh model guess elsewhere in the same file (see readLockedContext's docstring in decompose.mjs, reused by discovery.mjs's own resolveDiscovery per tsk-ozl D2).

ROOT CAUSE traced (this session, live-reproduced on tsk-3sw, not speculation): the overwrite happens because the tsk-ozl D2 skip shortcut (readLockedContext) is structurally dead code for the standard interactive workflow, in BOTH resolveDiscovery AND resolveDecompose -- so judgeDiscovery ALWAYS runs (never skipped), which is why its verify guess is always what reaches the overwrite site this item already describes.

Both resolveDiscovery (discovery.mjs:518-519) and resolveDecompose (decompose.mjs:438-439) compute 'const repoRoot = path.dirname(dir)' where dir is always the main checkout's .fgos (required by --dir, since worktrees never carry their own .fgos per ADR0020), then call readLockedContext(repoRoot, work.docsRef) -- a plain fs.readFileSync (no git-awareness) against path.join(repoRoot, docsRef). But fgos-exploring/fgos-planning write and COMMIT CONTEXT.md/plan.md to the item's OWN fgw/<id> branch/worktree (their own hard rule: commit before calling fgos discover) -- not to main, which has no idea those files exist until later merge. So readLockedContext always reads from the wrong physical directory and always finds nothing, in exactly the scenario (interactive session already did the real reasoning) the shortcut exists to serve. Confirmed live for tsk-3sw: after fgos-exploring committed CONTEXT.md and got contextApprove approved, 'fgos discover tsk-3sw' still spawned a full nested judgeDiscovery call instead of skipping, producing a wrong verify guess (a docs-grep check for what was really a code change) that had to be manually corrected -- this item's own overwrite bug, caught live in a second, independent real case.

Same session, 'fgos decompose tsk-3sw' independently confirmed resolveDecompose has the identical repoRoot bug (lockedContext empty -- confirmed by grepping plan.md/CONTEXT.md for 'tiny'/'small', zero matches, so decompose.mjs:469's mode-skip branch could not have fired) and fell through to a real judgeDecompose call (decompose.mjs:549, verdict.kind === 'pass-through') that happened to coincidentally agree with the human-approved plan -- luck, not a plumbing guarantee. Notably, decompose.mjs itself does NOT have this item's own overwrite bug: it computes planApproveVerify ONCE (line 431, gates[id].planApprove.verify ?? work.verify) and uses it unconditionally at every moveStage-to-executing call site (lines 469, 549, 597) regardless of skip-vs-real-judge path -- decompose.mjs already does correctly what this item's fix scope should make discovery.mjs also do.

Why the existing test suite (2366 passing) never caught the repoRoot bug: test/intake/discovery.test.mjs's own mkLockedContextFixture helper builds its CONTEXT.md fixture as path.dirname(storeDir)'s child -- deliberately constructing repoRoot == content-root by fixture design, with its own comment stating this 'exactly matches readLockedContext's real path.join(repoRoot, docsRef) resolution'. The fixture validates the function's internal logic in isolation; it never models the real git-worktree topology (state root always main per ADR0020, content root the item's own separate fgw/<id> checkout) that breaks it in production.

Widened fix scope (was discovery.mjs-only, now both files): resolveDiscovery AND resolveDecompose need to read CONTEXT.md/plan.md from the caller's actual live working directory (the worktree an interactive fgos-exploring/fgos-planning session is standing in) rather than deriving a content-root from the state-root dir/--dir -- likely an explicit separate parameter threaded through resolveDiscovery/resolveDecompose/readLockedContext, distinct from dir (which must keep resolving state from main per ADR0020). This item's own original fix idea (never overwrite a non-empty/non-placeholder work.verify) is a valid, narrower complementary guard -- but fixing repoRoot is the deeper fix, since it also restores the skip path's real purpose (avoiding the wasteful/context-blind judge call entirely, not just protecting verify from it). payload.title: Native-First Dispatch Doctrine Pha 2: caller-supplied verdict protocol for fgos discover/fgos
payload.description:
Native-First Dispatch Doctrine Pha 2: caller-supplied verdict protocol for fgos discover/fgos decompose, bypassing judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose's own blind subprocess judge when the caller already rendered a live decision. Real, concrete realization of the doctrine's rule 2 (native dispatch when caller is already a live same-provider soul) for this specific pair of engine verbs -- a bare CLI verb cannot itself call Task tool, so 'native' here means: let the caller (fgos-exploring/fgos-planning, running inside a live session that already did real Socratic/mode-gate reasoning) pass its own already-rendered verdict directly (e.g. --verdict clear --verify <cmd> for discover; an analogous shape for decompose's kind/child-split verdict), instead of the verb insisting on spawning its own context-blind judge. Stronger and more robust than tsk-1ni's file-detection fix (readLockedContext, fragile -- proven broken by a repoRoot/worktree path mismatch): an explicit flag from the caller can never silently fail to fire the way a heuristic file-read can. readLockedContext stays as a fallback signal for older/headless callers that do not yet pass an explicit verdict (e.g. the automated runner sweep, which genuinely has no live soul and must keep spawning a real judge). This is a CLI contract change (new optional flags on fgos discover/fgos decompose) -- needs its own clarify/plan/validate pass, not a quick patch alongside tsk-1ni's narrower repoRoot fix.

Footprint overlaps tsk-1ni's own fix (src/intake/discovery.mjs, src/intake/decompose.mjs) -- no hard logical dependency (tsk-1ni's repoRoot fix and this item's new explicit-verdict path are independent mechanisms achieving related goals), but sequencing after tsk-1ni avoids editing the exact same functions in parallel from two sessions. Also touches .claude/skills/fgos-exploring/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/fgos-planning/SKILL.md (and their .agents/ mirrors) -- they need to actually pass the new verdict flag once their own gate approves, instead of relying on CONTEXT.md/plan.md being committed+discoverable.

Part of docs/decisions/0026-vision-orchestrator-roottask-capacity-native-vs-cli-spawn.md (Native-First Dispatch Doctrine) -- Phase 2 of 5 in the implementation plan discussed for that doctrine. Phase 1 = tsk-1ni (repoRoot fix, ships independently). Phase 3 = tsk-53h (shared native-vs-cli/spawn detection helper for skill-facing capacity dispatch, different files, no footprint overlap, can run fully parallel to this item and to tsk-1ni). Phase 4 (unify capacities.<id> config dispatch with live Task-tool direct calls) depends on THIS item plus tsk-53h both landing first -- needs the concrete 'caller supplies its own verdict' pattern proven here before attempting the bigger, structural unification. payload.title: Native-First Dispatch Doctrine Pha 4: unify fgOS's capacities.<id> config-driven dispatch with a
payload.description:
Native-First Dispatch Doctrine Pha 4: unify fgOS's capacities.<id> config-driven dispatch with a live session's direct Task-tool subagent calls into ONE decision protocol. Today these are TWO fully separate mechanisms with zero shared decision layer: (1) src/runner/dispatch.mjs's capacities.<id> config path (resolveExecutorConfig/resolveCapacityCli/spawnWorker) -- always resolves to a real command/args, cli/spawn-shaped even for the new agentType branch (tsk-3sw); (2) a live session directly invoking the Agent/Task tool as one of its own tools -- entirely outside dispatch.mjs, never touches capacities.<id> config at all. The doctrine (docs/decisions/0026-vision-orchestrator-roottask-capacity-native-vs-cli-spawn.md, Native-First Dispatch Doctrine) says both are dispatching the same conceptual thing (a subTask or a capacity, from the activator's point of view -- same dispatch decision mechanism per that record's own corrected framing, subTask and capacity are NOT the same concept, only the dispatch mechanism is shared) and should go through ONE decision procedure (rules 1-4 in 0026), not two disconnected ones.

Real open design questions, NOT resolved here (deliberately, this item's own future clarify pass must settle them, per fgos-exploring's own material/grounded/answerable discipline -- not guessed at submit time): a bare CLI verb (dispatch.mjs, resolveExecutorConfig) structurally cannot call Task tool itself (confirmed multiple times this session, e.g. tsk-3sw's own D1 constraint) -- so unifying the two paths cannot mean 'make dispatch.mjs call Task' -- it must mean something like 'dispatch.mjs hands back a signal the calling session interprets and acts on itself' (an idea already floated and then simplified away during tsk-3sw's own design, see that item's 'Revised design' section) or 'the calling session consults a shared decision helper BEFORE choosing whether to shell out to dispatch.mjs at all or just call Task tool directly itself'. Which shape is right is exactly what this item's clarify stage needs to settle -- not assumed here.

Depends on tsk-27y (Native-First Dispatch Doctrine Pha 2, caller-supplied verdict protocol for fgos discover/decompose) AND tsk-53h (Pha 3, shared native-vs-cli/spawn detection helper for skill-facing capacity dispatch) both landing first -- this item needs the concrete 'caller declares/consults its own live-soul status' pattern proven on TWO separate real cases (the engine-verb case in tsk-27y, the skill-facing-helper case in tsk-53h) before attempting the bigger, structural unification across both dispatch.mjs's config path and direct Task-tool calls. Building this before either precedent exists risks designing an abstraction with no real proof it fits either concrete case. Phase 5 (agy native cross-provider) does not block or get blocked by this item -- orthogonal concern (which provider's native mechanism, not which of the two current dispatch PATHS to unify).

payload.description:

patch.description:
task-dispatch (in-session Agent/Task tool) has no path to a non-Claude backend at all -- Claude Code's own Agent/Task tool only selects among Claude models (opus/sonnet/haiku via an agent definition's model field), never an external CLI. So a cross-provider 'cheap capacity' need inside a live session cannot route through the Agent tool by construction; the only real mechanism is shelling out to an external CLI directly -- i.e. reusing cli-dispatch's own resolveCapacityCli/spawn mechanism via Bash, exactly what fgos-submit-assist's own classify step (tsk-5l2) already does once wired. This narrows the gap originally filed here (previously framed as 'task-dispatch needs its own separate architecture, distinct from cli-dispatch') -- it does not: task-dispatch for a Claude-family choice uses the Agent tool (agent definitions' own model field already covers this), task-dispatch for a cross-provider choice reuses cli-dispatch's existing spawn mechanism via Bash, same as fgos-submit-assist already proves works. The real, narrower gap: fgos-submit-assist is the only skill wired this way today -- there is no general, reusable pattern/helper any OTHER skill could follow to declare 'shell out to this capacityId via Bash if configured+present, else fall back to a real Agent/Task subagent spawn' without re-deriving fgos-submit-assist's own wiring from scratch. Scope: extract that pattern (a shared how-to or a small skill-facing helper) so future skills don't rebuild it ad hoc. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md (fgos-submit-assist's own real precedent to generalize from).

cli-dispatch <-> task-dispatch relationship (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the two are NOT two independent, parallel mechanisms -- they nest, asymmetrically. task-dispatch can always fall through to cli-dispatch (a live session always has Bash, so shelling out to a resolved capacity command is always available -- this is the D1 mechanism above). The reverse is conditional, not structural: cli-dispatch (fgos-runner, a bare Node process, never itself inside a Claude Code session) can never call the Agent/Task tool directly -- but if the specific command it spawns IS 'claude' itself (not a different CLI like agy/gemini), that spawned process is a REAL Claude Code agent loop, and task-dispatch (Task/Agent tool use) becomes available again one level down, inside that worker -- gated entirely by whatever --allowedTools the spawned invocation was given. Today's own committed .fgos-runner.json scopes every executor's --allowedTools narrowly (e.g. 'Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)' for the default worker) -- deliberately excluding Task/Agent tool access for spawned workers today, a config choice, not a hard technical wall. A CLI other than 'claude' (agy, gemini, ...) can never nest task-dispatch at all, regardless of config -- Task/Agent tool is specific to the Claude Code harness, not a generic capability other CLIs share.

Generalizing the nesting rule beyond Claude (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the "cli-dispatch spawns a real agent harness, so task-dispatch-like nesting becomes available one level down" property is not Claude-specific by nature -- it's just that Claude Code is the only harness fgOS currently knows to have it (via Task/Agent tool, gated by --allowedTools). agy/codex are already valid, ordinary cli-dispatch spawn targets today (agy is the running submit-assist-classify example; codex is already in KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES) -- that's their normal role, no special case needed. If either ever ships its own internal subagent/tool-dispatch mechanism (its own equivalent of Task/Agent tool), the same nesting principle would extend to it: that capability would become available one level down inside that spawn, gated by whatever permission/scope equivalent that harness exposes -- the fix would be recognizing it (mirroring how kind:"task" was carved out specifically for Claude's own mechanism in CAPACITY_KINDS), not redesigning the dispatch model. Not a need to build now -- pinned so a future session doesn't have to re-derive whether the nesting rule is Claude-only by accident or by design (it's the latter: Claude-only today because Claude is the only harness with the property, not because the rule itself assumes Claude).

Correction to the nesting framing above (discovered via 'claude --help'): cli-dispatch is not limited to nested one-level Task access via a plain 'claude -p' spawn -- 'claude' CLI has a real '--agent <agent>' flag ('Agent for the current session. Overrides the agent setting.'), letting cli-dispatch spawn 'claude -p --agent <name> ...' directly, running that named agent definition (.claude/agents/<name>.md, tsk-slq's canonical root) headlessly with no Task/Agent tool nesting needed at all. So for a Claude-family agentType capacity specifically, cli-dispatch and task-dispatch now converge on the SAME achievable outcome (right agent definition + right model on the prompt) -- native Task tool (when the calling session already has it) stays the cheaper/observable choice, but exec'ing 'claude --agent <name>' is always a correct, structurally-available fallback, not a degraded one. See tsk-3sw (dependency of this item) for the concrete resolveCapacityCli/resolveExecutorConfig change this enables.

Shared-helper format preference (decided in discussion, tsk-3sw's follow-on): prefer a single shared skill-facing fragment/reference file (e.g. under .claude/skills/_shared/ or equivalent canonical path) that consumer SKILL.md files point to by path, over each skill copy-pasting the branching prose into its own SKILL.md. Reason: N independent copies drift out of sync the next time this pattern's logic changes (DRY) -- a single referenced source doesn't. Sequencing: write this helper against tsk-3sw's finished resolveCapacityCli return shape (uniform {command,args,provider,model} for both cli and task kind, per tsk-3sw's current description) -- not before that lands.

UPDATE to 'Generalizing the nesting rule beyond Claude' above (real, verified evidence -- supersedes that paragraph's 'if either ever ships its own... mechanism' framing, which was written as a future hypothetical; it is NOT hypothetical, it already exists today): 'agy' (a real, installed, multi-provider CLI already used by submit-assist-classify) has its OWN native persona-dispatch mechanism, independent of Claude's. Verified live: 'agy --help' shows '--agent' flag and 'agent'/'agents' subcommands ('List available agents'). 'agy changelog' confirms: v1.1.1 added '--agent' flag + agent/agents subcommand; v1.1.6 added 'Custom Agents (Markdown Format)' -- agy's own 'agent.md' files, YAML frontmatter with fields 'mainAgent'/'subagent'/'hidden'/'inheritMcp'/'commandExecutionPolicy'/'model' -- a DIFFERENT schema than Claude's '.claude/agents/<name>.md' (name/description/model/tools). Ran live: 'agy --model gemini-3.6-flash-high --agent default -p "..."' -- works, self-identifies as running on Gemini 3.6 Flash under agy's 'default' built-in persona. 'agy models' confirms real multi-provider model list: gemini-3.x variants, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6-thinking, gpt-oss-120b -- all reachable through the same '--agent'/'--model' flag pair.

Implication: the canonical agent-definition root (agents/<name>.yaml, tsk-slq) now has a genuine SECOND real projection target, not just Claude's '.claude/agents/'. Both agy and claude happen to share the same CLI flag NAMES ('--agent <name>', '--model <name>') -- convenient but coincidental -- while their underlying agent-definition FILE SCHEMAS differ (Claude: name/description/model/tools; agy: mainAgent/subagent/hidden/inheritMcp/commandExecutionPolicy/model). Any capacity-dispatch design that resolves an 'agentType' into CLI args (tsk-3sw) must NOT hardcode Claude-only '--agent'/'.claude/agents/' assumptions -- it needs a per-provider mapping from canonical agent definition -> that provider's own adapter format and flag syntax, exactly the projection tsk-slq's design already anticipated, now with a real second target to build against instead of a hypothetical one. Not scoped to build now (still bigger than this item's own narrower helper-pattern scope) -- pinned so a future session sees this as confirmed fact, not speculation.

THIRD real per-provider agent-dispatch shape confirmed (user-provided, sourced from official Codex docs, spot-checked live: 'codex exec --help' shows no '--agent'/'--agenttype' flag at all, matching the claim) -- 'codex' (already in KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES, installed on this machine) has a STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT agent-dispatch mechanism than both Claude and agy: no CLI flag selects the agent at all. Persona dispatch happens via PROMPT TEXT naming the agent ('Use the reviewer agent to review this branch against main...'), after defining it in '.codex/agents/<name>.toml' (TOML, fields: name/description/model/model_reasoning_effort/sandbox_mode/developer_instructions -- a THIRD distinct schema, different from both Claude's .claude/agents/<name>.md (name/description/model/tools) and agy's agent.md (mainAgent/subagent/hidden/inheritMcp/commandExecutionPolicy/model)). Built-in agents (no file needed): default/worker/explorer. Model precedence per user's sourced docs: an agent file's own 'model' field wins over 'default_subagent_model' (a [agents] config default) when that agent is spawned as a subagent -- distinct question from '--model' on the top-level 'codex exec' invocation, which governs the orchestrating call, not the spawned subagent's own model choice.

This CORRECTS the earlier framing in this item ('Both agy and claude happen to share the same CLI flag NAMES --agent/--model -- convenient but coincidental') -- it is not even reliably a 2-provider pattern, let alone a convention: Codex breaks the 'flag selects the agent' assumption entirely. Confirms this item's own per-provider-mapping conclusion even harder: any capacity-dispatch design resolving an 'agentType' into real invocation args (tsk-3sw) cannot assume ANY common flag shape across providers -- Claude/agy need an '--agent <name>' arg substitution, Codex needs the agent name woven into the PROMPT TEXT itself instead (a fundamentally different code path: prompt-string composition, not argv-flag substitution). Reinforces tsk-3sw's own 'scope Claude-only now, file multi-provider as separate follow-on' recommendation -- a real per-provider adapter here is a 3-way branch, not a 2-way one, and not yet worth building without a concrete non-Claude agentType consumer.

Investigation shows this item's own declared footprint (src/intake/discovery.mjs, decompose.mjs, judge-executor.mjs) cannot host a real native-vs-cli/spawn decision.

judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose run inside runJudgeExecutor -> spawnAttempt -> spawnSync (a bare subprocess spawn, src/intake/judge-executor.mjs:417/188). This code path never has live Agent/Task tool access, whether invoked from a live session's Bash call or the headless runner sweep -- so calling decideCapacityDispatchMechanism (tsk-3ik-1) here would only ever pass hasLiveTaskAccess:false, which per that function's own logic can mathematically never return anything but 'cli-spawn'. Wiring it in at this level would be a dead, unreachable 'native' branch -- ceremony, not real behavior (fgos-executing's own no-pseudo-implementation rule).

The only place 'native' dispatch is actually achievable for judge-discovery/judge-decompose is the CALLING session (fgos-exploring/fgos-validating) -- and tsk-27y (Phase 2, already delivered) already built exactly that: both skills now self-supply their own verdict via 'fgos discover/decompose --verdict ...', bypassing judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose's subprocess spawn entirely whenever a live session already reasoned about it. Confirmed by reading resolveDiscovery (discovery.mjs:522-578): judgeDiscovery is structurally unreachable once a callerVerdict is supplied.

So the one remaining real wiring -- fgos-exploring's/fgos-validating's own SKILL.md gates calling 'decide judge-discovery/judge-decompose --has-live-task-access' before self-supplying their verdict, to formally tie their already-existing behavior to child 1's new decision helper -- touches a completely different footprint (skill files) than this item declared.

Which should this item do: (a) close as pass-through/no-op since tsk-27y already solved the real case and there's nothing left to build in this footprint, (b) expand this item's own footprint to also wire fgos-exploring/fgos-validating's SKILL.md gates, or (c) leave that SKILL.md wiring for a different item (e.g. tsk-3ik-4, the "document the convention" child) and close this one as-is?

payload.description: bug: judge subprocess calls (judgeDiscovery/judgeVerifySemanticCorrectness/judgeDecompose, invoked via fgos discover/fgos decompose) intermittently exceed a 2-minute wall-clock budget and get killed, even though a retry of the exact same call with a longer timeout succeeds in a few seconds. Reproduced twice during tsk-j7y: "fgos discover tsk-j7y --verdict clear --verify ..." timed out at 120s and was killed, then succeeded in under 4 minutes on retry with no code/state change in between; "fgos decompose tsk-j7y --verdict pass-through ..." did not reproduce this but was run with an extended timeout as a precaution after the discover case. This makes the CLI unreliable for callers using a default ~120s timeout (e.g. an interactive session's own tool-call timeout) even when the underlying judgment logic is correct and fast once it actually runs. Fix direction: investigate whether the judge subprocess has its own inconsistent startup/response latency (cold model connection, retry-without-backoff, etc.) and either fix the root latency cause or have the CLI itself report/retry more gracefully instead of silently hanging until an external caller's timeout kills it.

payload.title: Thống nhất dispatch của /fgOS:discover <id>, /fgOS:decompose <id>, và /fgOS:discover-next (dùng bởi
payload.description:
Thống nhất dispatch của /fgOS:discover <id>, /fgOS:decompose <id>, và /fgOS:discover-next (dùng bởi /fgOS:discover-loop) qua fgos-routing/fgos-coding-driving thay vì gọi verb CLI trực tiếp (mù, không --verdict, bật judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose subprocess không cần thiết khi có session sống).

## Bối cảnh / vấn đề hiện tại

Xác nhận qua đọc code trực tiếp (không suy đoán):

- plugins/fgOS/skills/discover/SKILL.md:45 -- /fgOS:discover <id> gọi thẳng bin/fgos.mjs discover $ARGUMENTS --json --dir ..., KHÔNG kèm --verdict -> luôn bật subprocess judgeDiscovery mù (không thấy hội thoại thật).
- plugins/fgOS/skills/decompose/SKILL.md:46 -- /fgOS:decompose <id> cùng pattern, cùng vấn đề.
- plugins/fgOS/skills/discover-next/SKILL.md bước 4 (dòng 52-57) -- sau khi pick item qua pickNextDiscoverItem, cũng gọi verb thẳng, mù.
- Đối lập: .claude/skills/fgos-exploring/SKILL.md:240 (+ mirror .agents/skills/fgos-exploring/SKILL.md) gọi discover ... --verdict clear --verify ... -- đây là đường ĐÚNG (session sống tự phán, hết mù), đạt được qua đi đúng cửa fgos-routing -> fgos-coding-driving -> fgos-exploring.
- --verdict flag caller-supplied đã có sẵn từ tsk-27y (xem docs/how-to/pass-a-caller-supplied-verdict-to-discover-or-decompose.md), engine không cần sửa gì -- chỉ cần đổi CÁCH các skill wrapper trên gọi verb.

## Phân tích thiết kế đã thống nhất trong phiên bàn luận trước

Nhóm A -- nên gộp qua routing (cùng scope stage clarify/decompose mà fgos-coding-driving đã quản):
- /fgOS:discover <id>, /fgOS:decompose <id> -- đổi thành: claim nếu chưa doing (fgos take --role session --id <id>), rồi load thẳng fgos-exploring/fgos-planning tương ứng (hoặc gọi fgos-coding-driving với ceiling: stage:decompose cho trường hợp clarify).
- /fgOS:discover-next (bước 4 trong discover-next/SKILL.md) -- GIỮ NGUYÊN bước 2 (pick qua pickNextDiscoverItem, src/state/discover-pool.mjs -- logic ordering này ĐÚNG, không đổi), chỉ đổi bước 4 từ gọi verb thẳng sang giao id vừa pick cho routing/fgos-coding-driving.
- /fgOS:discover-loop -- KHÔNG đổi gì, nó chỉ là /loop bọc discover-next lặp tới khi pool rỗng/lock-timeout -- thuần continuation, không đụng verdict/stage.

Nhóm B -- KHÔNG gộp, ngoài scope (để lại nguyên, không phải thiếu sót):
- /fgOS:cleanup-next/-loop, /fgOS:merge-next/-loop, /fgOS:retro-next/-loop -- xử lý status: cleanup/merge-ready/retrospective, các trạng thái này KHÔNG nằm trong stages array (clarify/decompose/executing) mà fgos-coding-driving quản lý theo D9/D10 (khoá trong .claude/skills/fgos-coding-driving/SKILL.md). Gộp nhóm này đòi hỏi mở rộng định nghĩa domain stage -- quyết định thiết kế riêng, lớn hơn, ra ngoài scope item này.

## Vướng mắc kỹ thuật cụ thể cần giải khi làm (đã xác nhận qua đọc src/state/discover-pool.mjs)

pickNextDiscoverItem trả về item ở CẢ 2 stage trộn chung 1 pool (không phải lỗi -- có lý do):
- frontier() (bộ chọn chính, executing-stage only) CỐ Ý loại trừ clarify/decompose (comment dòng 4-6 trong discover-pool.mjs) -- nếu discover-pool chỉ ôm clarify, item ở decompose sẽ không có sweep tự động nào, kẹt vĩnh viễn trừ khi gọi tay /fgOS:decompose <id>.
- Tên discover là tàn dư lịch sử: trước tsk-2b0, verb discover từng làm cả context-discovery LẪN split-work judgment trong 1 verb; tsk-2b0 tách verb ra (discover=clarify only, decompose=decompose only) nhưng pool/skill giữ tên cũ.
- Pool clarify LUÔN rút cạn trước decompose (dòng 65-69 + comment: clarify-stage ambiguity blocks everything downstream cho chính item đó, kể cả lượt decompose sau này) -- có chủ đích, giữ nguyên.

Hệ quả cho thiết kế route qua fgos-coding-driving: ceiling phải khác nhau tuỳ stage vừa pick -- pick clarify thì cần ceiling: stage:decompose (dừng ngay sau khi vượt qua clarify, KHÔNG để loop tự trôi tiếp sang xử lý decompose luôn trong cùng lượt); pick decompose thì có thể để mặc định/không ceiling vì mọi outcome của verb decompose đều tự thoát stage decompose theo 1 trong 3 hướng (pass-through->executing, need-human->awaiting-human, decompose->anchor bởi children) -- không cần ceiling riêng chặn thêm.

## Việc cần làm (để item con /plan xử lý, không quyết ở đây)

1. Đọc lại toàn bộ discover/SKILL.md, decompose/SKILL.md, discover-next/SKILL.md, fgos-coding-driving/SKILL.md (cả .claude/skills/ và .agents/skills/ mirror + plugins/fgOS/skills/) trước khi sửa -- xác nhận không có bản sao nào khác bị bỏ sót.
2. Thiết kế chính xác cách discover/SKILL.md/decompose/SKILL.md claim + dispatch qua routing (chọn 1: gọi thẳng fgos-exploring/fgos-planning, hay gọi fgos-coding-driving với ceiling phù hợp) -- cân nhắc chi phí: đổi từ one-shot mù, nhanh sang Socratic pass đầy đủ, chậm hơn, có thể hỏi lại user.
3. Sửa discover-next/SKILL.md bước 4: ceiling động theo stage vừa pick được (xem vướng mắc ở trên).
4. Cập nhật docs mô tả hành vi cũ: docs/how-to/advance-a-clarify-or-decompose-stage-item-with-discover-decompose.md:68, và bất kỳ chỗ nào khác reference hành vi one-shot cũ của 2 skill này (decompose/SKILL.md:8,25 tự sửa theo).
5. KHÔNG đụng cleanup-next/-loop, merge-next/-loop, retro-next/-loop -- ngoài scope (Nhóm B).
6. Cân nhắc: giữ lại đường mù cũ (gọi verb trực tiếp, không qua routing) như 1 cờ/flag riêng cho trường hợp headless thật (không có ai sống) -- hay bỏ hẳn, buộc luôn phải có session sống? Đây là câu hỏi cần chốt trước khi code (có thể là gray area cho fgos-exploring lúc clarify item này).

## Không thuộc scope item này (đã xác nhận, không cần bàn lại)

- Không đổi engine (src/intake/discovery.mjs, src/intake/decompose.mjs) -- --verdict flag đã hoạt động đúng từ tsk-27y.
- Không mở rộng stages array hay domain registry để ôm Nhóm B (cleanup/merge/retro).
- Không tự generalize fgos-coding-driving ra ngoài domain coding (D10 đã khoá).

## Unresolved questions

- Câu hỏi ở mục Việc cần làm #6 (giữ đường mù cho headless thật hay bỏ hẳn) chưa chốt -- cần quyết định trước khi implement, có thể để fgos-exploring/planning item con tự hỏi khi tới lượt.

Locked design: name follows fgos-coding-driving precedent since only the coding domain is real today (workflow-stage-graphs.mjs); does NOT duplicate fgos-exploring/fgos-planning authoring logic -- sets the item's refs field pointing at a scoped anchor inside DISCUSSION.md, then invokes fgos-exploring then fgos-planning directly in the same session (Native-First Dispatch Doctrine) once discussion converges; DISCUSSION.md is one file per feature with per-task anchors, sections: Muc tieu, Van de ro/chua ro, Quyet dinh da chot (D-IDs, append-only), Q&A log (append-only), Thiet ke da chot (regenerated each material change, coherent synthesis + diagram, sits before the task list), Danh muc hang muc/task (each with own goal, excerpt of Thiet ke da chot, applicable D-IDs, relations, draft verify); a current-status recap at top for multi-day resume; brainstorm loop is deliberately NOT Socratic-lock-per-answer (open prose, no AskUserQuestion forcing convergence each round) unlike fgos-exploring/fgos-planning -- D-ID only minted once a point is stable across rounds, matching Superpowers' hard rule that brainstorming's only allowed next skill is plan-writing; borrows scout-first and present-before-ask discipline from local ck:brainstorm skill but rejects its per-phase forced-decision-capture; one skill with two entry commands, no separate skill package, mirroring discover/discover-next and merge-list/merge-next; no new index file for child tasks -- reuse parent field + fgos rollup + plan.md's own split-list section, matching the zero-index-file precedent across all 162 existing docs/history/*/ folders. payload.description: Change HEAVY_KEYWORDS matching in classifyIronLaw (src/evolve/iron-law.mjs) and its keyword list (src/intake/risk-keywords.mjs) from plain substring match to word-boundary match. Bug observed on tsk-69g: classifyIronLaw's matchedFlags computation does description.toLowerCase().includes(keyword.toLowerCase()) for each HEAVY_KEYWORDS entry -- this matches 'auth' as a substring inside unrelated words like 'authoring', 'author', 'authentic', tripping the Iron Law gate (required: true, requiring --acknowledge-iron-law at approve time and a failing-test-first evidence doc) for diffs that have nothing to do with authentication/authorization. iron-law.mjs's own header comment already documents a related known limitation for matchedModules (illustrative, not exhaustive) but the matchedFlags substring behavior is a separate, independently fixable false-positive source. Fix: match each HEAVY_KEYWORDS entry against description using a word-boundary-aware check (e.g. a regex with \b boundaries, case-insensitive) instead of raw substring includes, so 'authoring' no longer matches keyword 'auth' but a real standalone mention of 'auth'/'authentication'/'authorization' still does. Scope: src/evolve/iron-law.mjs's classifyIronLaw function only -- matchedModules' path-prefix/equals matching is unrelated and out of scope. Existing tests for classifyIronLaw (iron-law.test.mjs or similar) must be updated/extended to cover both the false-positive-avoided case (a word containing a keyword as substring, not matching) and the true-positive case (the keyword itself, or with normal word boundaries, still matching).

patch.description:
resolveDiscovery (src/intake/discovery.mjs) has two 'trust the live session, skip the judge' paths that behave inconsistently. The lockedContext branch (tsk-ozl D2, committed CONTEXT.md trust signal) does an early return that skips BOTH judgeDiscovery AND the secondPass verify check below. The callerVerdict branch (tsk-27y D1/D2, 'fgos discover --verdict ...' -- the documented, official native-first entry point) sets verdict from the caller's own reasoning but does NOT early-return -- it falls through to the shared 'if (verdict.clear)' block, which runs judgeVerifySemanticCorrectness (a second subprocess LLM judge) against the caller-supplied verify string regardless.

This directly contradicts tsk-27y's own docstring intent (discovery.mjs ~line 528-535): 'a live session that already reasoned about clarity, fgos-exploring, should never fall through to either a blind subprocess judge or a second heuristic guess.' judgeVerifySemanticCorrectness IS that second heuristic guess -- it re-judges the verify command using only the item's title/kind/risk/tier (not the full locked CONTEXT.md reasoning), so it can dispute a verify string the calling session already justified with real evidence.

Reproduced live during tsk-1tm's own clarify pass (2026-08-04): three consecutive 'fgos discover tsk-1tm --verdict clear --verify ...' calls each got parked to awaiting-human via outcome:verify-disputed, each ~4 minutes (a real subprocess LLM call), even after CONTEXT.md's decisions were locked and approved -- because secondPass's own prompt has no access to CONTEXT.md's reasoning, only the item's raw fields. The eventual workaround was to drop --verdict entirely and call bare 'fgos discover <id>', which routes into the OTHER branch (lockedContext) and correctly skips both judges in one shot -- proving the fix belongs in the callerVerdict branch, not in crafting a 'better' verify string.

This matches a previously-noted, adjacent gap in the decision log (P25 dogfood run, 2026-07-16, item bo-hardcode-ten-trunk-main): 'buildDiscoveryPrompt chi dua title/kind/risk/refs/deps vao prompt, THIEU description day du + answer cua nguoi tu gates -> 2 vong hoi lap cung chu de roi fail-safe park' -- same class of prompt-context-starvation problem, this time hitting the secondPass judge specifically rather than the first-pass judge.

Suggested fix direction (not prescribing the exact code): either (a) have the callerVerdict branch early-return the same way the lockedContext branch does, skipping secondPass entirely when a live session already supplied a reasoned verdict, or (b) feed judgeVerifySemanticCorrectness the same locked-context evidence (CONTEXT.md content) the caller already reasoned from, so its dispute is actually informed instead of guessing from four bare fields.

payload.title: Cleanup stage lech khoi decision da khoa work-item-status-delivered-retrospective-cleanup o hai
payload.description:
Cleanup stage lech khoi decision da khoa work-item-status-delivered-retrospective-cleanup o hai diem doc lap. Day la restore-to-decision, khong phai thay doi thiet ke.

LECH 1 - TTL bi gop vao harness cua D8. D8 khoa dung HAI check cho cong cleanup->done: (1) code van con merged tren main, (2) retrospective that su tao ra noi dung. TTL KHONG nam trong hai check do. D7 dat TTL o vi tri khac han: no la thoi han park, mot tien de de duoc chay harness. Nguyen van D7: "run only after TTL elapses AND the cleanup->done harness (D8) passes" - hai ve noi bang AND. Implementation gop ca ba vao mot mang reasons trong assessCleanupReadiness (src/state/cleanup-harness.mjs:132), va bin/fgos.mjs case cleanup park sang blocked tren bat ky check nao fail.

Bang chung tu .fgos/events.jsonl: 6 vu cleanup->blocked trong toan bo lich su (tsk-3b3, tsk-1ca, tsk-3w3x, tsk-3o3, tsk-3xo, tsk-5y5). 6/6 co reason la TTL, 0/6 do check cua D8. Ca 6 hien van dang blocked, khong item nao tung recover. 4/6 bi park trong vong 3-20 giay sau khi vao cleanup. Vu moi nhat 2026-08-05T03:12:53. Day dung la trang thai ket ma D8 viet ro la "never a silent stuck state".

Hau qua may: blocked khong nam trong TAIL_RESOLVED_STATUSES (src/state/frontier.mjs:221, dung theo D13) nen item da merged bi tut tu resolved ve unresolved - statusCategory lat ve in-progress, dependent cho gia du code da tren main, va isCandidate cua cleanup-pool chi nhan status cleanup nen item khong bao gio duoc nhat lai.

Guard hien tai khong du: cleanup-pool.mjs duoc dung len (tsk-dvc) de ne dung bug nay, tu header module ghi ro vay. Nhung tsk-dvc delivered 2026-08-02T11:23:54, va 3/6 vu park xay ra SAU moc do (tsk-3o3 08-02T14:44, tsk-3xo 08-04, tsk-5y5 08-05). Guard dat o caller thi cac caller khac van bypass - trai voi one-door-write (CTR001).

LECH 2 - thu ma cleanup duoc giao bao ve da bi huy tu truoc. Pinned term cua cleanup trong CONTEXT.md: "a TTL-bounded park state for worktree reclamation, deliberately delayed (not synchronous with merge) so a post-merge incident can still reuse the worktree". Thuc te: cleanupMergedBranch chay ngay luc merge (bin/fgos.mjs:2632) va goi git branch -d; docstring cua chinh no ghi worktree checkout "normally already torn down by the runner at propose-time (loop.mjs finally)". Do tren du lieu that: 0/55 item dang o status cleanup con worktree, 1/55 con branch (tsk-47e - va dung cai duy nhat do lai la cai se fail check merge cua D8). plan.md:137-138 cua chinh feature nay da ghi phai doi call site removeWorktree/removeDispatchWorktree tu synchronous sang cleanup - chua lam, khong phai bi descope.

Nghia la voi domain coding - domain duy nhat dang chay that - stage cleanup hien chay rong. Khong phai stage vo dung: D5 khoa ro bon status la cong doan chung domain-agnostic, moi domain ap dung bien phap cleanup rieng qua harness/skill layer. Van de la bien phap cua domain coding chua duoc noi vao.

Chi phi dang tra: TTL 7 ngay x ~23 item delivered/ngay = khoang 160 item park thuong truc o cleanup. Hien khong mua duoc gi, vi Lech 2.

DA XEM XET VA BAC: them canh blocked->cleanup. D2 da can nhac va bac dung - duoi thiet ke khoa, cleanup->blocked chi no khi hong that, ma hong that thi hoac rework (->todo/doing) hoac bo (->wontfix); ca "park oan" khong ton tai. No chi ton tai vi Lech 1. Sua Lech 1 thi canh do thua, dung nhu D2 noi. Cuu 6 item ket dung blocked->delivered, chinh D2 dat ra lam mechanical retry.

Tach thanh 2 con: (1) tach TTL khoi harness D8, (2) doi diem huy worktree/branch ve cleanup. Con 2 phu thuoc con 1.

payload.description: judgeVerifySemanticCorrectness (src/intake/discovery.mjs, second-pass verify judge invoked via fgos discover) gives contradictory round-to-round verdicts on the same underlying claim, making clarify->decompose unreachable. Reproduced on tsk-4xg across 10 discover rounds: round 6 rejected a direct grep on a keyword as 'just word presence, too generic'; round 8 explicitly demanded that same direct-grep approach back; round 9 rejected a more specific phrase-grep as 'too specific, may miss other wording' (the opposite of round 6's complaint); round 10 rejected a runtime registry-structure introspection (checking DOCTOR_CHECKS/FIX_REGISTRATIONS array entries by id) as 'doesn't validate correct behavior', demanding e2e-level proof — but round 7 had already rejected referencing a not-yet-existing e2e test file for the same reason discover disputes any pre-implementation verify (item still at clarify, nothing built yet). No CLI escape hatch exists: fgos discover has no flag to accept/override a disputed second-pass verdict, and fgos edit --verify patches the field but does not itself fire the clarify->decompose transition (still gated through discover's judge call). Net effect: an item can get stuck in an awaiting-human/doing loop indefinitely with no way for a person to just accept a verify and move on, if the two judge passes never agree. Fix direction: investigate whether the second-pass judge's own prompt/context is unstable across repeated calls for the same item (e.g. missing memory of its own prior verdicts, or a prompt that lets it invent new unstated criteria each round), and/or add a person-facing override (e.g. fgos discover --verdict clear --verify ... --force, or accepting the item's already-recorded fgos answer text as authoritative) so a genuine two-judge disagreement doesn't strand an item forever.

payload.description:
Bug: ủa tại sao đang làm trên nhánh/worktree riêng thì lại bị block bở lock của main?

Hook .githooks/pre-commit (STR65 main-checkout lock) tự thiết kế chạy cho mọi git commit, kể cả trong worktree — không chỉ main checkout. Lý do: core.hooksPath là setting relative, khi git tự gọi hook cho lệnh commit trong worktree, nó resolve về bản .githooks/pre-commit ở main checkout (không phải bản trong worktree, vì worktree không có .fgos/ riêng theo thiết kế ADR0020). Nên hook đó check lock của main checkout thật, dù mình đang commit vào branch fgw/tsk-1p9 riêng, không đụng gì main.

Verify: comment gốc trong hook ghi rõ ý đồ "fires for ANY git commit against this checkout, regardless of actor... not only writes made through fgOS's own CLI verbs, per D2" — cố ý rộng vậy. Nhưng bản thân guard thứ hai trong cùng hook (currentFgwBranchIfMainCheckout) lại biết phân biệt worktree vs main checkout và bỏ qua worktree — riêng lệnh acquire-lock thì không có check tương tự, chạy vô điều kiện. Nhiều khả năng đây là gap thiết kế (lock áp cho worktree commit là thừa, vì worktree không đụng working tree của main), chứ không hẳn cố ý. Không phải việc của tsk-1p9/tsk-4jf để sửa — nêu ra để bạn biết, không tự ý mở rộng scope thêm.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

Finding (research, verify bằng lệnh thật + đọc code/docs, xem báo cáo đầy đủ tại plans/reports/internal-design-260805-1327-tsk-sir-worktree-commit-lock-scope-report.md):

1. Cơ chế thật: `core.hooksPath=.githooks` nằm trong `.git/config` DÙNG CHUNG mọi worktree (không phải per-worktree config). `git config --get core.hooksPath` chạy từ main checkout VÀ từ worktree tsk-1p9-rF2BQk ra CÙNG 1 đường tuyệt đối trỏ về main checkout's .githooks — verify trực tiếp, không đoán. Nên `.githooks/pre-commit` là 1 file vật lý duy nhất, `__dirname`/`repoRoot` trong nó LUÔN = main checkout, bất kể worktree nào gọi git commit.

2. Root cause thật của lock (decision docs/decisions/0021-wire-main-checkout-hook-qua-doctor-setup.md): bug tsk-3w8 — 1 session khác `git commit` tay lên MAIN cùng lúc approve's `mergeRunnerItem` cũng `git commit --no-edit` lên MAIN → main's `.git/index` bị clobber. Decision 0021 CHỈ bàn race trên main's index, KHÔNG hề nhắc worktree ở đâu cả.

3. Vì sao đây là gap thật, không phải chủ ý (3 bằng chứng, không chỉ suy đoán):
   - Mỗi linked worktree có `.git/index` RIÊNG (`.git/worktrees/<name>/index`), không đụng main's index — hazard thật (2 writer race trên CÙNG index) không áp dụng cơ học cho worktree commit.
   - Guard 2 trong CÙNG file (`currentFgwBranchIfMainCheckout`) biết so `git-dir` vs `git-common-dir` để phân biệt worktree/main và bỏ qua worktree. Guard 1 (`acquireMainCheckoutLock`, nằm ngay phía trên, cùng file cùng tác giả) không có check tương tự — bất đối xứng trong 1 file là dấu hiệu thiếu sót.
   - tsk-45y (task duy nhất từng bàn "cô lập .fgos per-worktree", đã đóng wontfix/resolved-by-context) bàn LỚP KHÁC — fgOS event-log writes (events.jsonl qua events.lock), chứng minh worktree không có .fgos ghi được để mà cô lập (ADR0020: dispatch worktree bị xóa .fgos, session/pick worktree chỉ symlink về store chung). tsk-45y's scout evidence (`rg -- "main-checkout-lock" src bin test docs`) KHÔNG grep `.githooks/` — chính nơi duy nhất lock này áp lên worktree commit. Nên tsk-45y không phủ nhận/giải quyết case này; nó có blind spot thật trong bằng chứng đóng của chính nó, chứ không phải đã xét rồi bác bỏ.

Đề xuất fix cho guard 1 (chưa implement, để fgos-exploring/fgos-planning tự khóa khi tsk-sir tới lượt):

Thêm cùng 1 check `gitDir !== gitCommonDir` (đã có sẵn logic này trong `currentFgwBranchIfMainCheckout`, cùng file) vào TRƯỚC bước gọi `acquireMainCheckoutLock` trong `main()` — nếu đang chạy từ 1 linked worktree (gitDir khác gitCommonDir), skip acquire/check lock, exit 0 luôn (giữ nguyên guard 2 vốn đã skip worktree). Lý do chọn hướng này thay vì sửa `acquireMainCheckoutLock` chính nó: hàm lock là primitive dùng chung nhiều call site khác (claim-port.mjs, merge.mjs) — chỉ call site trong hook mới cần phân biệt worktree, không nên đổi hành vi của primitive.

Rủi ro cần soi trước khi implement (không tự quyết ở đây):
- Có call site nào thật sự CẦN lock này áp cho worktree commit không (vd: 1 kịch bản race chưa lộ ra, nơi worktree commit vô tình đụng main checkout theo cách khác ngoài .git/index)? Chưa tìm thấy bằng chứng nào, nhưng chưa loại trừ hết.
- Cần regression test mirror shape của test hiện có cho guard 2 (kiểm tra worktree commit không bị chặn bởi lock khi main đang giữ lock, dùng git commit subprocess thật như test/e2e/main-checkout-lock-hook.test.mjs).
